+- **Evidence retention and reclamation** *(operator-ratified 2026-10-25, `RATIFY-WS58-RETENTION-LESSONS-20261025`)*: the
+  durability clause above says where evidence must live; this clause says what may not be removed
+  while it is still the only copy. It grants no reclamation authority to anyone. It bounds the
+  removals that other approvals authorise.
+  - **Homes.** Evidence behind a ratified or production-affecting claim lives under
+    `epyc-inference-research/data/<campaign>/` with a `SHA256SUMS` and a README. Design, decision
+    and review documents live in root `docs/` (`docs/design/`, `docs/reviews/`,
+    `docs/coordination/`) or in the owning handoff. Evidence for work in progress or a provisional
+    result may stay in scratch until the result is ratified, and is carried to its home then.
+    **Reproducible data is never carried**: worktrees, build trees, raw logs and downloads stay in
+    scratch, and a claim that cites one records it hash-and-provenance-only.
+  - **Durability classes.** This aligns the durability clause above with the operator ruling of
+    2026-08-03 that raw campaign data stays on local disk, gitignored. There are three classes:
+    - *carried-in-git*: tracked and reachable from a pushed ref;
+    - *durable-untracked*: the bytes sit under `epyc-inference-research/data/<campaign>/` on this
+      host, gitignored, and are covered by a `SHA256SUMS` that is itself carried in git;
+    - *hash-and-provenance-only*: the bytes are not kept; the SHA-256, size, collection recipe and
+      provenance are.
+    The first two satisfy "inside a repository" above. A durable-untracked artifact has no
+    off-host copy.
+  - **The reclamation predicate binds every reclaimer**: an interactive session, a wrap-up
+    cleanup, a trash sweep, an approved volume reclaim and an autonomous loop alike. A path under
+    `/mnt/raid0/llm/tmp`, `/mnt/raid0/llm/worktrees`, `/mnt/raid0/llm/.trash` or
+    `/mnt/raid0/llm/state` may be removed only when ALL of these hold:
+    1. **Not cited.** No record cites it. The citation sources are: root handoffs (active and
+       blocked, on `origin/main` and in the working tree); the compute queue (FILLERS, grants and
+       launchers); the canonical belief ledger; the research registry; AutoKernel campaign
+       inputs; the scratch manifest; the session bus; the observer registry; and crontab. A cited
+       path becomes removable only after it is promoted to its home and every citing record is
+       re-pointed (`REPOINTED from`), or after it is de-cited. **No removal may take the sole copy
+       of a cited artifact.**
+    2. **Not KEEP-marked.**
+    3. **No size threshold.** Size is a reported column only. No keep-or-remove verdict reads it.
+    4. **Fail-closed.** A citation source that cannot be read makes the verdict UNVERIFIABLE, and
+       an unverifiable path is kept.
+    5. **Re-checked at every step.** The citation check runs at plan time, again at execute time,
+       and again on the original path at purge time.
+    6. **Trash first, then held.** Removal moves the path to the trash. A trashed entry is purged
+       no sooner than 7 days after trashing. A batch approval does not shorten the hold. Only an
+       exact-path, per-entry approval with a clean re-check does.
+    7. **Explicit target.** Exact paths only: no glob, pattern, `find -delete` or listing-driven
+       sweep.
+    8. **Tombstone before unlink.** The purge record is written and fsynced before anything is
+       unlinked. It carries the original path, a SHA-256 computed immediately before removal, the
+       size, and the approval it acts under.
+  - **Three states, not two.** A verifier distinguishes three cases for a cited artifact:
+    present and hashing correctly is *conforming*; absent with a tombstone is *expected
+    absence*; absent without a tombstone is a *defect*. A defect is reported as an incident,
+    never left as a silent gap.
+  - **Scope and enforcement.** The autonomous-loop expiry grant drafted on 2026-08-03
+    (`artifacts/operator/autokernel-policy-draft/evidence-retention.draft.md` §3.2-§3.7) is not
+    enacted by this clause. Until it is, loop reclamation is governed by this predicate like any
+    other. The enforcers are the guards named in `agents/shared/OPERATING_CONSTRAINTS.md` →
+    *Destructive operations* and `epyc-inference-research/scripts/validate/check_evidence_durability.py`.
+  *Origin: the 2026-10-25 reconciliation (`docs/reference/tmp-loss-reconcile-2026-10-25.md`) found
+  244 real losses among 497 handoff-cited `/mnt/raid0/llm/tmp` paths. The 2026-10-20 volume reclaim
+  skipped its citation check for every entry under 0.02 GiB, which covered 72 of the 73 cited paths
+  it removed. A follow-on script then purged that batch out of the trash within two minutes. §6
+  already pointed here, but the clause had never been written.*
